root_cause.text: The V3D compute-shader dispatch path failed to treat zero workgroup counts as a no-op, allowing indirect CSD jobs to reach hardware with a zero in CFG0/CFG1/CFG2 where the driver should have rejected or short-circuited them.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an early return in `v3d_csd_job_run()` when any `V3D_CSD_QUEUED_CFG{0,1,2}_NUM_WGS_{X,Y,Z}` field is zero, and it moves the indirect workgroup-count overwrite in `v3d_rewrite_csd_job_wg_counts_from_indirect()` so the job’s CFG registers are updated even if counts are zero; the commit message states that “Kicking off a dispatch with a zero count in any of the three dimensions is invalid” and such a case “should only result in a no-op.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject compute shader jobs with zero workgroup dimensions so they are not incorrectly dispatched to hardware.
intent_record.what: A new early-return check was added in v3d_csd_job_run() before the job is marked active. The added code inspects the X, Y, and Z workgroup count fields in job->args.cfg[0..2] using V3D_GET_FIELD(), and returns NULL if any of those dimensions is zero. A comment explaining the hardware/user-space zero-versus-65536 interpretation was also inserted above the check.
intent_record.how: At runtime, compute shader dispatches with a zero workgroup count in any dimension are now skipped instead of being submitted to hardware. This prevents the driver from treating a zero-sized workgroup dimension as the hardware's encoded value of 65536 and avoids dispatching a shader job when user space intended no workgroups.

intent_record.intent_summary: Populate the CSD configuration from indirect work-group counts before bailing out on zero-sized dispatches.
intent_record.what: The zero-check for `wg_counts[0..2]` was moved from before the `args->cfg[0..2]` assignments to after them; the assignments now always execute before the function may jump to `unmap_bo`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the work-group counts are now written into `args->cfg` even when one of the indirect counts is zero, whereas previously those fields were left unset in that case. The early exit on invalid/empty counts still occurs, but only after the configuration words are populated.

candidates.rationale: This is the pre-fix zero-workgroup check in the indirect compute dispatch path; the vulnerability arises because zero counts could still proceed further into hardware submission instead of being safely treated as a no-op or rejected early.

This branch shows the old handling path for zero-sized indirect dispatches, but the bug indicates the driver did not correctly short-circuit the job before hardware programming, allowing invalid zero CFG values to reach the device.

This statement advances the compute-shader job into the active hardware queue; if zero-workgroup jobs are not rejected before this point, they can be dispatched to hardware despite being invalid/no-op.

This is the pre-fix control-flow target for zero-sized indirect dispatches, and the bug was that such jobs could still proceed into hardware submission with zero CFG values instead of being safely short-circuited.

This statement moves the compute-shader job into the active queue; if zero-workgroup jobs are not rejected before this point, they can still be dispatched to hardware despite being invalid or a no-op.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact indirect CSD workgroup-count handling in `v3d_rewrite_csd_job_wg_counts_from_indirect()`. The vulnerable construct is present in the conditional `if (wg_counts[0] == 0 || wg_counts[1] == 0 || wg_counts[2] == 0)` which previously did `return;`, meaning zeroed workgroup counts were not treated as a proper no-op/cleanup path. However, in this commit the code has already been fixed: the early return was changed to `goto unmap_bo;`, and the `unmap_bo:` label ensures both `v3d_put_bo_vaddr(indirect);` and `v3d_put_bo_vaddr(bo);` are always executed. So the zero-workgroup case is handled correctly here, and the leak/faulty early-exit behavior is no longer present.
